items.prompt: White to move. Follow the opening habits: take space in the centre or bring a piece out.

claims.statement: Bb5, d4, Bc4 and Nc3 are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.

hints: Which of your pieces are still on the first rank? Which has a free diagonal?
A bishop move to b5 or c4 develops and eyes the black knight or the f7 pawn.
Bishop to b5 or c4, knight to c3, or the d-pawn two squares.
items.explain: Each of these moves develops a piece or takes space in the centre. At depth 16 the engine puts them within 40 centipawns of one another.

items.prompt: Black to move. Black has not castled yet. Is castling sound right now? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Castling is within 40 centipawns of the best move.

hints: Is any black piece loose (attacked and not defended)?
Does White threaten anything that castling would ignore?
items.explain: No black piece is loose, and castling is legal. At depth 16 the engine rates it within 40 centipawns of its best move, d6.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's last move was e5. Is castling sound right now? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Castling is at least 300 centipawns worse than the best move.
d5 and Ng4 are within 40 centipawns of the best move.
One white piece (the e5 pawn) attacks f6.

hints: What does the pawn on e5 attack?
Is Black's knight on f6 defended well enough?
items.explain: The pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6, so castling lets White take it. At depth 16 the engine rates castling at least 300 centipawns below its best moves, d5 and Ng4.

feedback_by_move.e8g8: It ignores the attack on f6: exf6 wins a piece. The engine rates castling at least 300 centipawns below the best moves.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has just retreated the knight. Is a habit the answer here, or something else?

claims.statement: Nc6+ is the engine's first choice; Ng6+ is the other move that wins material, within 400 centipawns.

hints: Look at the file between the white queen and the black king.
A knight on e5 can move with check because the queen stands behind it.
items.explain: The knight leaving e5 uncovers a check from the queen, so its own move comes with tempo. Nc6+ also attacks the queen; the engine rates it far above everything else at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Choose a good move.

claims.statement: d4, d3 and b4 are within 40 centipawns of the best move.
O-O is at least 30 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Think about what castling leaves behind.
items.explain: Castling is the habit, but here it leaves the e4 pawn loose: the knight on f6 attacks it and nothing defends it. The engine rates castling below d4, d3 and b4 at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.e1g1: The habit, but ...Nxe4 comes at once. The engine rates it at least 30 centipawns below the best moves at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Choose a good move.

claims.statement: Nxd4 and Bc4 are within 40 centipawns of the best move.

hints: A black pawn has just captured in the centre. Can you take it back?
Or develop a piece with a plan to take it back later.
items.explain: Nxd4 takes the centre back and develops a knight in one move. At depth 16 the engine puts it first, with the gambit move Bc4 within 40 centipawns.
